<details>
This is a font-repackaging PKGBUILD. All ten sources are pinned: the two `Xmind[wght]` variable fonts and the OFL license come from `raw.githubusercontent.com/google/fonts` at a fixed commit (`_gfcommit`), the Nerd Fonts `FontPatcher.zip` comes from the official `ryanoasis/nerd-fonts` release tagged `v3.5.1`, and the remaining five entries (`make_statics.py`, `make_features.py`, `set_gasp.py`, `measure.py`, `README.md`, `FEATURES.md`) are local files expected to sit next to the PKGBUILD in the AUR repo. The build logic is ordinary packaging work: it optionally cuts static instances with fontTools, optionally runs the extracted upstream `font-patcher`, then runs `ttfautohint`, optionally applies a `gasp` tweak, and installs the resulting TTFs plus the license into `$pkgdir`. The inline Python heredocs are trivial and benign: one sets `head.flags |= 1 << 3` (the documented "integer ppem" bit) on the just-built fonts, another prints family names for fontconfig generation. There is no `eval`, no base64/hex/octal-obfuscated blob, no `curl`/`wget` piping into a shell, no download from an unexpected host, and no access to anything outside `$srcdir`/`$pkgdir` (the `rm -rf` targets are the package's own staging directories).

That is a rendering tweak consistent with the package's stated purpose, not a system-wide hijack.

Hygiene notes (not threats): the helper Python scripts and docs are unpinned from any upstream VCS but are covered by checksums here, so their integrity depends on the AUR repo itself — normal for maintainer-supplied build helpers; `parallel --will-cite` is a harmless nag-suppression flag. Nothing deviates from ordinary AUR font packaging.
